hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad: I heard a man asking Abdullah ibn Abbas about the spoils of war (al-anfal). Ibn Abbas said: 'The horse is from the extra reward, and the personal belongings taken (from the enemy) are from the extra reward.' Then the man repeated the question, and Ibn Abbas said: 'That also.' Then the man said: 'The anfal which Allah the Blessed and Exalted mentioned in His Book, what are they?' Al-Qasim said: He continued asking him until he almost embarrassed him, so Ibn Abbas said: 'Do you know what the example of this is? His example is like the example of Dabi' whom Umar ibn al-Khattab struck.'

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُصْعَبٍ ، قَالَ : حَدَّثَنَا مَالِكٌ ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ ، عَنْ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : سَمِعْتُ رَجُلًا ، يَسْأَلُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَبَّاسٍ ، عَنِ الأَنْفَالِ ؟ فَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ : الْفَرَسُ مِنَ النَّفَلِ ، وَالسَّلَبُ مِنَ النَّفَلِ ، قَالَ : ثُمَّ أعَادَ الرَّجُلُ الْمَسْأَلَةَ ، فَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ : ذَلِكَ أَيْضًا ، ثُمَّ فقَالَ الرَّجُلُ : الأَنْفَالُ الَّتِي قَالَ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى فِي كِتَابِه مَا هِيَ ؟ قَالَ الْقَاسِمُ : فَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَسْأَلُهُ ، حَتَّى كَادَ أَنْ يُحْرِجَهُ ، فقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ : هَلْ تَدْرُونَ مَا مَثَلُ هَذَا ؟ مَثَلُهُ مَثَلُ ضَبِيعٍ الَّذِي ضَرَبَهُ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُصْعَبٍ ، قَالَ : حَدَّثَنَا مَالِكٌ ، عَنْ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ يقول : كَانَ النَّاسُ إنما يُعْطَوْنَ النَّفَلَ مِنَ الْخُمُسِ

hadiths.english_translation: It reached him that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz used to say: 'It reached me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: For the horseman, two shares, and for the foot soldier, one share.'

chainIssues: Double mursal (disconnection): First, from Malik using 'balaghahu' (it reached him), meaning he doesn't name his source for what Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said
Second mursal: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz himself uses 'balaghani' (it reached me) without naming who told him about the Prophet ﷺ
Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz was born around 61-63 AH, after the Prophet's death (11 AH), making this definitely mursal

plainChains: Malik -[unknown intermediary]-> Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz -[unknown intermediary]-> Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

potential_issues.issue: Malik uses 'بلغه' (it reached him) without naming his source for what Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said
potential_issues.impact: This creates a disconnection in the chain. We don't know who transmitted Umar's statement to Malik. However, Malik was extremely careful about his transmissions, and such mursal reports from Malik are considered strong among mursal narrations.

potential_issues.issue: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz uses 'بلغني' (it reached me) without naming his source from the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: This is a mursal report. Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz was born decades after the Prophet's ﷺ death and never met him. He doesn't name the companion or narrator from whom he received this report. Mursal narrations are considered weak in transmission, though some scholars accept mursal reports from reliable successors (tabi'in) like Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who was known for his piety and knowledge.
The combination of two mursal transmissions makes this chain significantly weak from a technical isnad perspective, despite the high reliability of both Malik and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz as individuals.

hadiths.arabicText: بلغه أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ ، كَانَ يَقُولُ : بلغني أن رسول الله صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، قال : لِلْفَارَسِ سَهْمَانِ ، وَلِلرَّجُلِ سَهْمٌ

hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: 'And I view the camels, cattle, and sheep to be in the status of food, which the Muslims eat from when they enter the land of the enemy, just as they eat from the food. And if that were not to be eaten until the people attend the divisions and it is divided among them, that would harm the armies. And I see no harm in what is eaten from all of that in a reasonable manner. And I do not see that anyone should store any of that to return with it to his family.'

hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ مَالِك : إن وَأَنَا أَرَى الْإِبِلَ ، وَالْبَقَرَ ، وَالْغَنَمَ : بِمَنْزِلَةِ الطَّعَامِ ، يَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ ، إِذَا دَخَلُوا أَرْضَ الْعَدُوِّ ، كَمَا يَأْكُلُونَ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ ، وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ لا يُؤْكَلُ حَتَّى يَحْضُرَ النَّاسُ الْمَقَاسِمَ ، وَيُقْسَمَ بَيْنَهُمْ أَضَرَّ ذَلِكَ بِالْجُيُوشِ ، وَلَا أَرَى بَأْسًا بِمَا أُكِلَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ عَلَى وَجْهِ الْمَعْرُوفِ ، قال : وَلَا أَرَى أَنْ يَدَّخِرَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْئًا ، يَرْجِعُ بِهِ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ

hadiths.arabicText: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو مُصْعَبٍ ، قَالَ : حَدَّثَنَا مَالِكٌ ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : بَعَثَ سَرِيَّةً فِيهَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ قِبَلَ نَجْدٍ ، فَغَنِمُوا إِبِلًا كَثِيرًا ، وَكَانَت سُهْمَانُهُمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ بَعِيرًا ، أَوْ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ بَعِيرًا ، وَنُفِّلُوا بَعِيرًا

hadiths.arabicText: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو مُصْعَبٍ ، قَالَ : حَدَّثَنَا مَالِكٌ ، عَنْ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : قَدِمَ عَلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ مَالٌ مِنْ الْبَحْرَيْنِ ، فَقَالَ : مَنْ كَانَ لَهُ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَأْيٌ ، أَوْ عِدَةٌ ، فَلْيَأْتِنِي ، فَجَاءَهُ جَابِرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ، فَحَفَنَ لَهُ ثَلاثَ حَفَنَاتٍ

hadiths.english_translation: Malik was asked about a leader who accepted the jizyah (tribute) from a people, and they were paying it. 'What do you think about whoever becomes Muslim among them - does his land remain his, or does it become for the Muslims, and does their wealth become theirs?' Malik said: 'That differs. As for the people of peace treaty (ahl al-sulh), whoever becomes Muslim among them has more right to his land and his wealth. As for the people of conquest by force (ahl al-'anwah) who were taken by force, whoever becomes Muslim among them, his Islam protects his life, but his land becomes fay' (public property), because the people of conquest have been overcome in their lands, and it became fay' for the Muslims. As for the people of peace treaty, they are a people who protected their lands, their wealth, and themselves until they made peace over them, so there is nothing upon them except what they made peace over.'
